item.title: New Adaptive Estimators for FIR System Identification Achieve Asymptotic Efficiency Without Noise Knowledge
item.description:
New Adaptive Estimators for FIR System Identification Achieve Asymptotic Efficiency Without Noise Knowledge

Researchers have introduced a new class of adaptive estimators for identifying finite impulse response systems under unknown or heavy-tailed noise conditions. The approach, published on 25 Nov 2026, aims to overcome limitations of classical estimators like least squares (LS) and least absolute deviations (LAD), which are sensitive to outliers or statistically inefficient when noise characteristics deviate from their assumptions.

🧩 How it works

The proposed method leverages kernel density estimation to construct two nonparametric maximum likelihood-type estimators: the estimated maximum likelihood estimator (eMLE) and the estimated profiled MLE (epMLE). These estimators approximate the likelihood using residuals from consistent initial estimates, thereby avoiding parametric assumptions on the noise distribution.

⚙️ Key details

The approach includes the following components:

  • Two adaptive estimators: eMLE and epMLE
  • Kernel density estimation for nonparametric likelihood approximation
  • Use of residuals from consistent initial estimates
  • Mild regularity conditions for theoretical guarantees
  • One-step Newton–Raphson algorithms for computational efficiency
  • Asymptotic normality and consistency
  • Achievement of the Cramér–Rao lower bound
Estimator Description
eMLE Estimated maximum likelihood estimator
epMLE Estimated profiled MLE

🚀 Availability

The paper is available on arXiv under the category of Electrical Engineering and Systems Science > Systems and Control, submitted on 25 Nov 2026.

💡 Why it matters

Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed methods outperform classical LS and LAD estimators in both robustness and accuracy, often matching oracle MLE performance across various noise distributions.

Source: Asymptotically Efficient Finite Impulse Response System Identification without Noise Knowledge

item.title: New AI development in linear system identification
item.description:
New AI development in linear system identification

A new approach to kernel-based regularization for linear system identification has been introduced, focusing on stability-compatible kernels and non-Gaussian priors.

🔍 Overview

  • Kernel-based regularization uses positive semidefinite kernels to define RKHSs and as covariance models for stochastic impulse responses.
  • Sharp kernel conditions are known for RKHS stability, but almost-sure BIBO stability under Gaussian priors requires more restrictive conditions.

🧩 How it works

  • The new approach introduces stability-compatible kernels, which admit at least one stochastic realization with almost-surely absolutely summable sample paths.
  • Stability-compatibility holds if and only if the stable elements are dense in the associated RKHS, a condition weaker than RKHS stability.
  • Practical sufficient conditions, including a spectral criterion for stationary kernels, are derived.
  • Non-Gaussian priors are constructed to preserve a prescribed covariance while enforcing almost-sure stability.

⚙️ Key details

  • The approach yields a stable prior based on the stationary radial-basis-function (RBF) kernel, separating covariance structure from the mechanism enforcing stability.
  • Numerical experiments show substantial estimation gains for several important classes of impulse responses, with particularly pronounced advantages when relevant dynamics occur at late lags or in separated temporal regions.

💡 Why it matters

  • The new approach provides a more flexible and stable framework for linear system identification, with potential applications in various fields.
  • The separation of covariance structure from the mechanism enforcing stability offers a novel perspective on kernel-based regularization.
  • The practical sufficient conditions and the stable prior based on the RBF kernel could lead to improved estimation and modeling in various scenarios.

#AI #MachineLearning #SystemIdentification #KernelMethods #Stability

Source: Stability-compatible kernels: beyond Gaussianity for impulse response estimation
